name: Toasted
blocked: Olo storefront (toasted.olo.com, channel 'toasted', location 'toasted-del-mar' -- address confirmed matches 12925 El Camino Real) gates its menu API behind a JS-issued anti-forgery token: /api/vendors/toasted-del-mar returns 403 {"error":"Anti forgery validation failed"} even with cookies from a prior GET. No token visible in HTML or the Next.js chunks (grepped all 7 JS chunks for AntiForgery/CSRF/RequestVerificationToken, none found) -- needs a real browser to complete the handshake. The restaurant's own site (toastedgastrobrunch.com/Menu) lists full dish names for the Del Mar location's breakfast/waffle sections but publishes no per-item prices (tag-stripped text has exactly one dollar figure on the whole page, a +$9.50 shrimp add-on). FINDINGS.md documents a prior capture of this restaurant's Toast/Olo catalog with a clean 'A LA CARTE' menu alongside a marked-up 'Delivery Brunch' menu (1.10x) -- that capture is not reproducible from this environment.
notes: Needs a Chrome-equipped agent to load https://toasted.olo.com/menu/toasted-del-mar, let the SPA fetch its own anti-forgery token, then read window state or network responses for the menu JSON.

name: Carmen's Mexican Food
blocked: Two disagreeing tier-5 third-party listings, neither dated. allmenus.com (Grubhub-owned, curl-verified with a Googlebot UA -- server pre-renders for crawlers -- tag-stripped text confirms 107 priced items, e.g. Beef Tacos (2) $7.95, Carne Asada Burrito $9.00) and menucollectors.com (independent owner, also curl-verified) price overlapping items 10-40%+ higher and inconsistently (Beef Tacos (2) $9.95, Carne Asada Burrito $11.50) with no uniform ratio across items, so it is not a clean delivery markup either -- it looks like two different, unreliable snapshots. FINDINGS.md records a prior pass on this restaurant that found a first-party photo of the printed menu dated 2018 (now known stale) plus one third-party listing 40-50% higher, and concluded the higher/newer listing should be trusted -- but that reasoning assumed one dated source vs one undated source. Here there are two undated third-party sources disagreeing with each other, which is a different situation: no source here is confirmed current.
notes: Neither allmenus nor menucollectors carries a visible date. The restaurant's own site (carmensmexican.com) is a template with a #menu anchor and the text 'Menu and prices subject to change. Call restaurant for current prices' -- zero prices in the HTML. Did not find the 2018 photo referenced in FINDINGS.md (not re-searched due to time) or any dated dine-in artefact. Uber Eats returns 403 to both curl and WebFetch. No DoorDash listing found via WebSearch. Recommend a Yelp photo search for a dated printed menu, or a phone call, to resolve which price level is current.

name: Dairy Queen

FINDINGS.md documents a DIFFERENT DQ branch (Chula Vista) blocked by a closed-store price gate at night; that does not apply here since this store is open, but the block is different: the ordering flow is a Next.js SPA whose menu data comes from a GraphQL BFF at https://prod-api.dairyqueen.com/graphql/ (found in __NEXT_DATA__ as NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_URL). name: Pho Royal
notes: FINDINGS.md records this restaurant as a prior fabrication case: its PDF menu is pure image (2 bytes of text), and its own domains (phoroyal.com, orderphoroyal.com) and Menufy storefront carry dish names/branding but zero prices -- all reconfirmed here (phoroyal.com/menu: 0 dollar-figures in tag-stripped text; orderphoroyal.com/order: Menufy 404). The only priced source found is DoorDash's server-side schema.org Menu JSON-LD (82 items across 8 sections), which is NOT the same failure mode as the PDF -- verified by parsing the actual <script type="application/ld+json"> block, not a WebFetch summary. Address matches (6937 Federal Blvd = 6937 Federal Boulevard; DoorDash lists it as Lemon Grove, CA -- same location, our work-list entry just omits city). Markup test clean: no divisor (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25) produces a round-number pattern; 71/82 prices end in .95 (organic POS pricing). CAUTION: the 'Pho' section holds exactly 1 item (Beef Noodle Soup $7.50) for a restaurant literally named Pho Royal -- this may be a genuine hybrid Vietnamese/Chinese-American menu (the catalog is heavy on Kung Pao/Orange Chicken/stir-fry, which is common at these hybrid pho shops) rather than a missing core section, but it could not be confirmed against a dine-in artefact -- own site and Menufy have no prices to check, and no independent second source (Grubhub's page was a client-rendered shell with no JSON-LD or SSR content) was reachable to corroborate. Sections captured: Appetizers, Pho, Vermicelli Noodle & Rice Entree, Chicken, Vegetarian, Featured Item, Vietnamese (banh mi sandwiches), House Specials.

blocked: Two ordering platforms, both dead ends without a browser. (1) The own-site 'order online' link goes to clover.com/online-ordering/mariscos-mazatlan-hhh-escondido, which per playbook is Clover's hosted COLO2 React SPA -- confirmed by fetching the page: it loads window.APP_CONFIG-driven bootstrap JS with no server-rendered content and an empty #root div. The WordPress moo-clover REST path does not apply here (mariscosmazatlanhhh.com/wp-json/moo-clover/v1/categories returns 404 rest_no_route -- this restaurant is not running the WP plugin). (2) A Toast storefront also exists (order.toasttab.com/...) and was fetched with a Chrome UA -- window.__OO_STATE__ is present and parses cleanly (address confirmed: 1111 E Washington Ave, Escondido, CA 92025, guid fe92f364-9f5f-4a3c-b480-130e1f340450) but its Apollo cache holds only restaurant metadata (name, location, cuisine, hours config) with zero menu/item/price keys -- this is a client-side-fetch deployment per PLAYBOOK.md's note that some Toast pages embed the full catalog and others don't. Postmates (postmates.com/store/mariscos-mazatlan/...) 404s to curl; Grubhub's restaurant page is a client-rendered shell with no JSON-LD or SSR content.
notes: Needs a Chrome-equipped agent on either the Toast storefront (read the client-side GraphQL response for the menu after it loads) or accept that Clover COLO2 has no known server-side workaround and is a dead end regardless of browser.

name: Tilted Stick
blocked: Own site (tiltedstick.online) is behind a full Cloudflare JS challenge -- confirmed both by direct curl (403, Cloudflare challenge HTML) and via r.jina.ai proxy (also 403'd with the Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge page), so it is not merely a curl-UA problem. Two curl-verified tier-4/5 sources agree on a LOW price level: SinglePlatform (singleplatform.com/tilted-stick-the/menu, schema.org Offer JSON embedded in the page) prices 1/3 lb. Burger $6.00, Double Burger $8.00, 2 Mahi Tacos $8.50; allmenus.com (Googlebot UA, item-title/item-price spans in the rendered HTML) prices Burger $7.25, Double Burger $9.50, 2 Mahi Tacos $9.00 -- different owners, same ballpark, satisfying the tier-5 two-independent-sources rule for those items. BUT WebSearch summaries citing Postmates/Uber Eats (which curl 404s and WebFetch 403s on this host, so unverifiable byte-for-byte) report the SAME items 40-90% higher: BBQ Stick Burger $12.00, Bacon Cheez Burger $15.50, Double Burger $17.00. That gap is too large and non-uniform to be a delivery markup (BBQ Stick ratio ~1.55x, Bacon Cheez ratio ~1.82x against the closest allmenus analogues) and reads instead as the staleness pattern documented for Carmen's Mexican Food in FINDINGS.md: a newer source disagreeing upward is ordinary, meaning the low, curl-verified SinglePlatform/allmenus figures are very likely outdated even though they agree with each other.
notes: Neither the low pair nor the high pair can be fully trusted: the low pair is internally consistent but plausibly stale (both are the kind of restaurant-submitted/aggregator data the playbook already flags as often years old), and the high pair could not be verified against raw bytes because Postmates/Uber Eats 403/404 both curl and WebFetch from this environment. Needs a Chrome-equipped agent to either get past the Cloudflare challenge on tiltedstick.online directly, or load the Uber Eats / Postmates listing to confirm today's real prices byte-for-byte.

name: Sammy's Woodfried Pizza
blocked: Every reachable source is marked up, and the own-site/first-party sources are unreachable. Own site (sammyspizza.com) is Cloudflare-gated (403 to a Chrome UA on both the homepage and its Location-Details page). The restaurant's own Olo storefront (sammyswoodfiredpizza.olo.com/menu/sammys-san-marcos-2) uses the same serve-next architecture as Toasted's Olo storefront in this same batch -- __NEXT_DATA__ pageProps is empty, items are fetched client-side behind an anti-forgery-gated API, not reachable by curl. Two delivery channels ARE reachable and both confirmed address-matched (121 S Las Posas Rd, San Marcos, CA 92078): Slice (__SLICE_REDUX_STATE__, 75 priced items after dropping a 'Non Display Products' entry) and DoorDash (schema.org Menu JSON-LD, 84 items). DOORDASH FAILS THE MARKUP TEST CLEANLY: dividing DoorDash prices by 1.10 lands 54/72 non-'Most Ordered' items on an exact whole or half dollar with zero exceptions among the ones checked in detail (Kobe Beef Chili 15.40->14.00, Mini Duck Tacos 22.00->20.00, Lamb Chops 38.50->35.00, Oak Roasted Salmon 35.20->32.00, etc) -- a textbook 10% online-ordering surcharge. Slice's 28 overlapping items are consistently BELOW DoorDash's (never above) by a non-uniform 3-8%, which rules out Slice being the clean base too -- it reads as a smaller, separate markup on the same underlying menu, not the true price.
notes: Per playbook: the markup test tells you a source is unusable, not what the real price was -- did NOT construct or report the divided-back (/1.10) numbers as dish prices even though they land suspiciously clean. Needs either the Cloudflare-gated own site or the anti-forgery-gated Olo storefront via a real browser to get a first-party number, or a dine-in menu photo (Yelp has 579 photos for this restaurant, not searched due to time).
